finding.text: At 400 the library is one 9.3-screen column and the collection filter (ui · figma) sits *below* the stage, so a phone user sees the item before the way to choose one (layout: order, flow) — layout.json library band share 9.298 at 400; shots/…-framework-library/400.png, band 3 (chips at y≈660, under the stage). The brief says "mobile first": the rails want to be a horizontal strip (or a sheet) on mobile, with the filter on top.

At 1920 and 3440 the 400-wide render sits flush left in a stage box that spans the whole centre column, leaving ~60–75% of the stage empty (sizing) — shots/…-library/1920.png and 3440.png, centre band; layout.json empty 0.762 / 0.825. Centre the render in the stage, or let the stage hug it.

`optimalWidth` exists only as collection defaults (ui 400, figma 1920); no template sets its own yet, and the "filter by 3440" grid and the span-by-width preview rule are recorded in doc/decisions.md §5 but not built (rails are one column). Acceptable for the first slice; the brief's "one preview layout rule" is only the zoom rule so far.

The page's level-1 line is missing: the constructor has a good description ("Everything we built, browsable: pick one on the left…") but the shot shows only "Library", then "ui figma", then a "UI" label — a newcomer is not told what the three columns are (content 1) — shots/…-library/1200.png, top band. The "ui" chip and the "UI" rail title also repeat each other.

The padding contract's red flag is never seen on the site: it is proved by a headless test only (readme "Watch out"), and the assembler refusal is deferred — both stated honestly in doc/decisions.md §7.
The "media" variant thumb is mostly a blank grey block at every width (its image placeholder) — shots/…-library/1920.png, right rail band 2; it reads as a broken preview.
